definitions.explanation: Not treating people or things equally or justly. Describes situations, rules, or treatment that favor one side over another.

examples.japanese: それは{不公平|ふこうへい}だ。
{不公平|ふこうへい}な{扱|あつか}いを{受|う}けて、{怒|おこ}りを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt angry at being treated unfairly.

examples.japanese: {税金|ぜいきん}の{負担|ふたん}が{不公平|ふこうへい}だという{声|こえ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many voices saying the tax burden is inequitable.

notes:
USAGE:
The antonym is {公平|こうへい} (fair, impartial). Both are very common in everyday conversation and formal discourse.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不公平|ふこうへい}な{扱|あつか}い (unfair treatment)
- {不公平|ふこうへい}な{制度|せいど} (unfair system)
- {不公平|ふこうへい}{感|かん} (sense of unfairness)
